items.title: Is Big Tech’s AI slowdown a safety pact or a cartel?
items.summary: When OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Google DeepMind cofounder Demis Hassabis, and SpaceX head Elon Musk loosely agreed over the weekend to slow down AI development, skeptics spotted an ulterior motive immediately. The AI titans had declared that their aim was to "pace the frontier," signing on at least partially to a proposal for embedding third-party auditors, regulating domestic labs, and reaching a global slowdown agreement. Their critics, however, argued they simply wanted to stop would-be competitors, kneecap the open-source movement, and avoid real legal safeguards - some dubbed it an outright "cartel." items.title: Australia politics live: Labor defends Catherine King’s top-tier Qantas membership gift; defence recruitment reaches 16-year high
items.summary: Follow the day’s news live Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast The South Australian premier, Peter Malinauskas, says there is optimism that steel making will continue in his state, after the closure of a major blast furnace at Whyalla was announced yesterday. Speaking to ABC News Breakfast from Whyalla and donned in some hi-vis, Malinauskas says there was disappointment, heartbreak, but also a sense of inevitability when the announcement was made. [Whyalla] has the capacity to be a viable operation but it hasn’t been recapitalised. The blast furnace is over 60 years old. It was first built in 1965 and blast furnaces of this age not to be realigned on a frequent basis. This hasn’t been done in 20 years. The fact it’s still going is a miracle. We need to have the plant recapitalised and that’s exactly the plan we have in conjunction with the federal government … if we lose this capacity behind me, this country doesn’t have structural steel-making capacity and we can’t afford that. If Pauline Hanson wants to take us down the road of Americanising our politics, so people in a family who disagree on political issues can’t speak to each other any longer, this is the pathway to do it … We’ve got lots of challenges facing Australia, but we’re not going to solve them by punching down on things that are brilliant about our country. So I think it’s rotten. I think it’s awful. I think it’s ugly. I just don’t agree with those comments. But I actually do agree with Senator Jacinta Nampijinpa Price when she says that there are serious issues that do need to be discussed. And these comments shouldn’t be a distraction from them. I mean, why aren’t we closing the gap? Continue reading...

items.title: 봉화서 전소된 승용차 안 40대 남성 숨진 채 발견
items.summary: 경북 봉화에서 불에 탄 승용차 안에서 40대 남성이 숨진 채 발견돼 경찰이 조사에 나섰다.15일 경북소방본부 등에 따르면 전날 오전 8시19분쯤 봉화군 석포면에서 직장 동료인 40대 남성 A 씨가 출근하지 않는다는 신고가 경찰에 접수됐다.신고자는 A 씨의 승용차가 전소된 채 발견된 사실도 경찰에 알린 것으로 전해졌다.공동 대응 요청을 받고 현장에 출동한 소방 당국은 불에 탄 차량 내부에서 A 씨가 숨져 있는 것을 발견했다.차량은 2020년식 아반떼로 전소됐으며, 당시 119에 별도의 화재 신고는 접수되지 않은 것으로 파악됐다.소방 당국은 인력 28명과 장비 11대를 투입했으며, 경찰은 정확한 화재 원인과 A 씨의 사망 경위 등을 조사하고 있다.(봉화=뉴스1)

items.title: 통영 갈도 해상서 어선 전복…6명 구조-1명 심정지

articles.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 14일 샤브카트 미르지요예프 우즈베키스탄 대통령과 만나 “교통, 인프라, 보건의료, 기후위기 대응, 핵심광물 공급망, 인공지능(AI)과 방위 산업에 이르기까지 호혜 협력의 지평을 넓히고 미래성장동력을 함께 이끌어갈 수 있다고 믿는다”고 밝혔다.이 대통령은 이날 오후 청와대에서 진행한 미르지요예프 대통령과의 정상회담에서 “양국 사이에 쌓인 우정과 신뢰를 토대로 특별 전략적 동반자 관계를 한층 내실 있게 발전시키고, 공동 번영과 평화를 향해 함께 도약하기를 바란다”며 이같이 말했다.이 대통령은 “특히 우즈베키스탄은 20만에 이르는 고려인 동포들이 삶의 터전을 일궈온 매우 각별한 나라”라며 “어려웠던 시절에 우리 동포들을 따뜻하게 품어주신 우즈베키스탄 국민 여러분께 늘 고마운 마음을 간직하고 있다는 점을 말씀드린다”고 전하기도 했다.미르지요예프 대통령도 “전자 정부, 교육, IT, 농업, 보건의료를 비롯한 산업에 전반 걸쳐 한국의 경험과 기술이 폭넓게 공유되고 있다”

articles.title: Ancestors review – messy but moving ghostly drama about the Aids crisis
articles.snippet: Toronto film festival: Saipan standout Éanna Hardwicke is a soulful gay man looking for a missing friend in a striking yet muddled debut It’s not normal to regularly contemplate mortality in your twenties, to ask questions about where we might go after we die and whether any part of our legacy will even matter in the years following. But for gay men in the 1980s, death was everywhere. In David Turpin’s intermittently impactful debut Ancestors, the director tries to make a connection with those men who lived through the very worst years of the Aids crisis. Turpin, born in 1982, might not have the first-hand experience but he bears the scars passed on from generation to generation and like many young gay men coming of age in the years after, likely experienced a watered down version of the shame and fear those before him once felt.
